The "NOT REJECTED" items are mostly my harness's classification bug (labels starting with "valid"/"host bits"/"empty" were passed to expect_invalid). Looking at the code: `if label.startswith("valid")` → expect_valid else expect_invalid. The labels "addr ...", "host bits", "empty fib", "empty bursts", "no cases" went to expect_invalid but they're valid requests. My classification is wrong, not the compiler.

Two real findings:
1. "addr ::1/0128" was NOT rejected — leading zero in the prefix length! The protocol says L is "decimal 0..128, without leading zero except '0'". So "::1/0128" must be INVALID. Wait, my regex `_LENGTH = re.compile(r"0|[1-9][0-9]*\Z")` — "0128" doesn't match `0` (because of \Z) and doesn't match `[1-9][0-9]*` (starts with 0) → should be rejected. Hmm, but `re.match` vs `fullmatch`: I used `_LENGTH.match(...)` and the pattern ends with `\Z` → equivalent to fullmatch ✓. So "0128"... `0|[1-9][0-9]*\Z`: alternation binds loosely — the pattern is `0` OR `[1-9][0-9]*\Z`. With re.match and no \Z on the first alternative, "0128" matches the alternative `0` (just the first char) → accepted ✗ BUG!

Fix: use `(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)\Z`.

2. "fe80:0000:...:0001/128" with leading zero groups → valid IPv6 (leading zeros in hextets are allowed) → NOT rejected ✓ my harness wrongly listed it under addr-invalidation. Actually I put it in the "invalid addresses" list. The protocol only forbids leading zeros for the prefix length ("without leading zero except '0'" refers to L). For addresses, "either letter case" and standard forms — leading zeros in a group are legal IPv6 text. So accepting it is correct. I'll move it to the valid list.

So the real bug is #1. Let me fix the regex and re-check.

Also let me fix my harness classification: use explicit (label, payload, expect) tuples.
